title: The Missing J: compact monthly reader panel
source_title: The Missing J in Interwar Europe: A Monthly Cliometric Dataset on Effective Exchange Rates and Trade-Balance Adjustment, 1925–1936
extraction: Exact source cells selected with the Python csv module; no numerical parsing, rounding, interpolation, row filtering or imputation.
missing_values: Empty CSV fields preserve the original missing-value representation. Boolean eligibility flags are the original True/False strings.
scope: The 28-country source grid is broader than the 18-country European baseline. Baseline lagged annual rates begin in 1928, using annual weights available from 1927. Some macro variables and rate constructions are missing for individual countries or months.
estimation: The compact file retains every input required to reproduce baseline local projections and the separate calendar-alignment audit. It omits alternative effective-rate designs and raw historical inputs, so it is not the full source-reconstruction archive.
reported_estimates: Paper figures and source result tables retain the submitted estimates. The separately labeled calendar audit documents the submitted code’s screened-row lag/lead convention and a strict calendar-date sensitivity check.
units: Trade series are nominal seasonally adjusted source values. Effective-rate increases mean depreciation. Reported local-projection responses are 100 times log changes for a +0.10 log depreciation, commonly described as approximate percent responses to a 10% depreciation.
